subtitle: An invitation for Elif — Would you like to …?
canDo: I can invite someone and answer an invitation.

Kibar ret kalıbı çok önemli: "I'm afraid I can't" + sebep. Türkçede kısaca "Gelemem" demek normal; İngilizcede sebep ve teşekkür beklenir.
Rol oyunu: bir öğrenci davet etsin (Would you like to…?), diğeri önce kabul etsin, sonra başka bir davete kibarca hayır desin.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: What is Thanksgiving?
sections.intro: A short guide for new students at Harbor English School.
paragraphs: Thanksgiving is one of the biggest holidays in the United States.
It's always on the fourth Thursday of November, and schools and most offices are closed.
On this day, families and friends eat a big dinner together.
The most famous dish is turkey, but people also eat potatoes, corn and a lot of vegetables.
For dessert, there's usually pumpkin pie.
Before dinner, many families go around the table, and everyone says what they are thankful for: their health, their family, their friends.
It's also a very busy time for travel. Millions of people drive or fly home to see their families.
In New York, there's a big parade in the morning, and in the afternoon, a lot of people watch American football on TV.
For people who live far from home, like students, friends often become their family on Thanksgiving.

options: on the last Friday of November
on the fourth Thursday of November

sections.title: Grammar: invitations, offers and suggestions
look: **Would you like to come** to dinner?

head: You want to …
You say …
Answers
rows: **Would you like to** come to dinner?
I'd love to! / Thanks, but **I'm afraid I can't**.
**Can I** bring anything? / **Shall I** make a dessert?
Yes, please! / No, thanks. That's OK.
**Let's** make baklava! / **Why don't we** meet at six?
Good idea! / OK, let's do that.

rules: **Would you like to** + verb? = a polite invitation. (not *Would you like come?*)
**I'd love to!** = yes (very friendly). **I'm afraid I can't.** = no (polite).
**Let's** + verb, no *to*: Let's go! · **Why don't we** + verb?: Why don't we go by bus?
When you say no, say why: *Sorry, I'm afraid I can't. I'm working that day.*
examples: Would you like to come to my party?
I'm afraid I can't. I have a concert.
Let's meet at the café at six.

support.tr: Davet: Would you like to + fiil? = …-mek ister misin? (Would you like to come? = Gelmek ister misin?) Kabul: I'd love to! = Çok isterim! Kibar ret: I'm afraid I can't = Maalesef gelemem, ve bir sebep. Öneri: Let's + fiil = Hadi …-elim (Let's go! = Hadi gidelim!). Teklif: Can I / Shall I bring something? = Bir şey getireyim mi?
support.ar: الدعوة: Would you like to + الفعل؟ = هل تحبّ أن …؟ (Would you like to come? = هل تحبّ أن تأتي؟). القبول: I'd love to! = يسعدني ذلك! الرفض المهذّب: I'm afraid I can't = للأسف لا أستطيع، مع ذكر السبب. الاقتراح: Let's + الفعل = هيّا نـ … (Let's go! = هيّا بنا!). العرض: Can I / Shall I bring something? = هل أُحضر شيئًا؟

tr.note: Would you like'tan sonra to + fiil gelir; Let's'ten sonra to yok.
wrong: Would you like come to dinner?
Let's to go to the park.
right: Would you like to come to dinner?

ar.note: لا تستخدم to بعد Let's، وعند الرفض لا تقل No فقط: قل I'm afraid I can't واذكر السبب.
right: I'm afraid I can't come. I'm working.
